title: Renfe starts notifying customers of a September data breach
date_note: Date of Renfe's individual notices to travellers as reported by Público; the unauthorised access Renfe dates to 24 September 2026 and it made the incident public on 28 September.
geo_basis: country as stated; Madrid used as the national point
summary: Renfe says a third party gained unauthorised access to some of its corporate systems on 24 September 2026. Público reports Renfe is now sending individual notices saying the data involved includes names and contact details, DNI, NIE or other identity document numbers, ticket purchase and travel history, and encrypted account passwords. Renfe says it has no evidence of fraudulent use. Público says the Guardia Civil detained a suspect in October 2026.
plain: Spain's rail operator Renfe is writing to travellers about a September breach that, it says, involved names, contact details, ID numbers, ticket history and encrypted passwords.
exec: A national rail operator's customer data, including ID document numbers, is involved; phishing and impersonation risk for travellers.
action: If you have a Renfe account, change its password and any reused one; do not share passwords or codes by email, SMS or phone; questions to dpdviajeros@renfe.es.
impact: Customer personal data involved; the notice as reported gives no number of people.

validation.note: Público (20 Nov 2026) relaying Renfe's notice; no second publisher read in this run.
